agree.reason: Speaking as a neighbour who will also sit at the slower light makes the speech credible and may move an undecided commissioner, but it does nothing to shrink the traffic cost, so the two commissioners worried about traffic and the opposed neighbours have little new reason to change their minds.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but a few details are added: 'I drive through that intersection all the time', the 'working families, seniors, and people starting over' description, and calling a D rating 'a little longer some mornings', which plays down a rush-hour rating.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are mostly repeated rather than worked: the speech never spreads 310 trips across a day (about 13 an hour, or under 5 per unit), never says the project would house about 16% of the 412 households on the waiting list, and states 72 spaces only as 'more than one each'.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative plainly: the paved lot stays empty six days a week and 412 households keep waiting three years, though it doesn't show what happens to the shortage if nothing is built.

qualification.reason: This is an advocacy speech with no conditional promise, and the honest point that 64 homes won't close the gap needs no checkable hedge.

objections.reason: It takes on the traffic objection first and directly, and answers the parking worry with the 72 spaces, but it meets the traffic concern mainly by conceding it rather than using the trip numbers to show the cost is small.

fit.reason: At about 420 words it fits a three-minute public comment, uses a spoken register, and opens and closes in proper form for the commission.
